import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 421

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/421](https://www.erdosproblems.com/421)
-/

open Set

namespace Erdos421

/--
Is there a sequence $1 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots$ with density 1 such that all products
$\prod_{u \le i \le v} d_i$ are distinct? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_421 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (d : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono d ∧ 1 ≤ d 0 ∧ HasDensity (Set.range d) 1 ∧
    {(u, v) : ℕ × ℕ | u ≤ v}.InjOn fun (u, v) => ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc u v, d i := by
  sorry

end Erdos421

Its update of 1 September 2026 cites Pratt’s simplified proof exposition, following an approach sketched by Tao, developed by Chojecki, and subsequent independently claimed AI-assisted proofs. Pratt’s exposition follows the proofs of Chojecki and Sneiderman.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/421 explicitly states “The answer is yes” and links https://www.erdosproblems.com/static/421-Pratt.pdf. Theorem 1.1 of that exposition asserts the existence of a natural-density-one set whose distinct nonempty consecutive blocks have distinct products, exactly the property asked for here.
